events.title: Pre-meeting staff briefing on mixed risk balance
events.expected_impact: May reinforce a pause baseline while preserving room for internal debate and possible dissent management.

events.title: Drafting session for statement language emphasizing optionality
events.expected_impact: Supports institutional coherence, reduces market overreading, and lowers the chance that public communication outruns the actual vote.

events.title: Dovish faction circulates downside-risk memo before final deliberation
events.expected_impact: Modestly raises salience of a follow-on cut case and increases the chance of a dovish dissent or more accommodative statement language, even if the median remains inclined to pause.

events.title: Rates desks reprice toward pause-with-dovish-watch
events.expected_impact: Marginally reinforces pause as the market baseline, while keeping volatility around dissent and guidance elevated.

events.title: Commentary focus pivots from headline rate call to dissent map
events.expected_impact: Raises salience of internal division and path dependence without requiring a dramatic change in headline odds for January.

events.title: Growth-focused analyst note on hold-vs-cut distinction
events.expected_impact: Sustains public pressure for responsiveness to growth risks while reducing narrative confusion about the endpoint; may slightly raise salience of dovish dissents more than the base rate of an actual cut.

events.title: Inflation-focused analysts circulate pre-meeting caution note
events.expected_impact: Slightly raises public salience of hold arguments and reinforces hawkish-caution framing, with more effect on dissent interpretation than on any guaranteed headline outcome.

events.title: Hawkish bloc circulates pause-first talking points
events.expected_impact: Marginally strengthens the hold camp among uncertain median participants and may reduce the odds of an immediate cut while keeping dissent risk contained.

simulation_brief.summary: A rate-setting committee approaches its January 28, 2026 meeting after a December cut. Internal uncertainty is elevated, with mixed risk assessments and plausible dissents in either direction. The operative endpoint is narrow: a 'yes' requires the target range to be lower immediately after the January statement than immediately before the meeting. A hold with dovish language still resolves to no.
simulation_brief.core_tension: Whether recent easing and mixed inflation/financial-condition signals lead to another immediate cut or a pause.
simulation_brief.decision_rule: endpoint turns yes only on an actual lower target range at the January 28, 2026 meeting statement.
uncertainty_notes: Source packet is sparse and mostly describes policy posture rather than detailed macro data.
Exact committee composition, voting blocs, and external macro surprises are not provided.
Dissents are plausible in either direction, implying non-unanimity risk without fixing the outcome.

risk_flags.description: Corpus lacks detailed inflation, employment, and financial-condition data that would strongly anchor vote dynamics.

Scenario centers on a real public institution but does not require targeting or persuasion; no fictional substitutes used for the main committee.
One OASIS interaction edge references policy_commentariat, which is represented as a cohort not an actor; downstream validation may need normalization.
